headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0189 — SMTO can't use this file type for this step

html:
SMTO-EXE-0189 — SMTO can't use this file type for this step

GUID: 9c48ada5-2482-578c-ad55-8e0a131c6d1c
Slug: office-unsupported-format
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • The file isn't a type SMTO's document tool works with for this step, or the file types don't match, such as a Word step on an Excel file or a picture that isn't PNG or JPEG. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the file ends in .doc, .xls or .ppt, or ends in .docm, .xlsm or .pptm, open it in Word, Excel or PowerPoint and use Save As to save a .docx, .xlsx or .pptx copy. SMTO edits only the standard modern formats, and files with macros can only be inspected.
  2. Make sure you ask for a step that matches the file, for example a spreadsheet change for an .xlsx file. SMTO won't use its Word tools on a spreadsheet or its Excel tools on a document.
  3. If you gave SMTO a name for the new file, make it end the same way as the original, for example report-new.xlsx for an .xlsx file. SMTO saves Word, Excel and PowerPoint files only with their own matching ending.
  4. When adding a picture to a slide, use a PNG or JPEG file. Save other pictures as PNG first. SMTO only inserts PNG and JPEG pictures.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the step and reports the new file it created with the right ending.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file names you used, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An Office operation received an unsupported or mismatched format: a source suffix other than .docx/.docm/.xlsx/.xlsm/.pptx/.pptm, a tool for a different format, an output_path whose extension differs from the produced format, or a non-PNG/JPEG image for slide insertion.

What this means

  • Package inspection, format-specific editing, output extension or image insertion received an unsupported or mismatched file format. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Package inspection, format-specific editing, output extension or image insertion received an unsupported or mismatched file format.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare actual package format, requested Word/Excel/PowerPoint operation, output suffix and image type.

How to fix it

  • Use .docx, .xlsx or .pptx sources with the matching word_/excel_/powerpoint_ operation (.docm/.xlsm/.pptm are inspect-only); legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt must be converted first. An explicit output_path must end in .docx, .xlsx or .pptx matching the format, and powerpoint_add_image accepts only real PNG or JPEG files.
  • Use supported matching Office formats and output suffixes; image insertion accepts PNG/JPEG. Macro-enabled documents remain inspection-only.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use .docx, .xlsx or .pptx. Macro-enabled .docm, .xlsm and .pptm support inspection only.

How to verify the fix

  • The source, operation and new output extension agree; inserted images use supported PNG/JPEG formats.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
